name: Uniform Point Cloud Voxelization and Simplification
body: A preprocessing technique to simplify large point clouds by voxelizing them and randomly sampling points within voxels to a target density, followed by re-projecting the simplified points onto multi-planes for aggregation weight calculation. It sets itself apart from sibling hard voxelization methods by introducing a probabilistic downsampling step based on local point density, rather than deterministic retention or max-pooling, and immediately projects the result into a multi-plane representation for subsequent neural rendering. Inputs: Point cloud: N points with 3D coordinates (x, y, z). Voxel parameters: sidelen (voxel size in meters), numineachvoxel (target points per voxel). Camera parameters: Intrinsic matrix K, Extrinsic matrix E (camera-to-world), image dimensions w \times h. Depth bounds: validdepthnear, validdepthfar. Multi-plane parameters: numplanes (default 32). Outputs: Simplified point indices and associated metadata for multi-plane aggregation. Data structures: usorted (uint16), vsorted (uint16), dposition (uint8), validposition (uint32), groupseach (uint32), groupsindex (uint32), groupseachindex (uint16), spliteachbegin (uint32), spliteachbeginingroup (uint32), spliteachmax (uint16), distance (float16), delta (float32). Data Structures: The output is organized into groups corresponding to voxels in the projected 2D space. groupseach: Array of size numplanes, storing the number of points in each plane's voxel grid. groupsindex: Flattened list of point indices belonging to each group. distance: Depth of each point (float16). delta: Weighting factor for aggregation (float32). Steps: 1. Bounding Box Calculation: Compute the bounding box of the input point cloud: \text{min}x, \text{min}y, \text{min}z, \text{max}x, \text{max}y, \text{max}z 2. Voxel Index Assignment: For each point i with coordinates (xi, yi, zi), compute the linear voxel index: \text{num}x = \lceil \frac{\text{max}x - \text{min}x}{\text{side\len}} \rceil \text{num}y = \lceil \frac{\text{max}y - \text{min}y}{\text{side\len}} \rceil \text{idx}i = \text{rint}\left(\frac{xi - \text{min}x}{\text{side\len}}\right) + \text{rint}\left(\frac{yi - \text{min}y}{\text{side\len}}\right) \cdot \text{num}x + \text{rint}\left(\frac{zi - \text{min}z}{\text{side\len}}\right) \cdot \text{num}x \cdot \text{num}y where \text{rint}(\cdot) denotes rounding to the nearest integer. 3. Sorting: Sort all points by their computed voxel index \text{idx}i to group points belonging to the same voxel together. 4. Probabilistic Sampling: For each contiguous block of points with identical voxel indices: Let C be the count of points in the current voxel. Let T be the target number of points (numineachvoxel). Calculate selection probability for each point in the block: p = \frac{T}{C} Generate a random uniform number r \in [0, 1) for each point. Select the point if p > r. 5. Re-projection to Multi-Planes: Calculate the transform matrix: M = K \cdot E^{-1}. Project 3D points to 2D image coordinates (u, v): u = \frac{x}{z}, \quad v = \frac{y}{z} where z is the depth relative to the camera center. Filter points based on valid image bounds (0 \le u < w, 0 \le v < h) and depth bounds (validdepthnear < depth < validdepthfar). 6. Depth Filtering: Sort valid points by depth in descending order. Remove outliers: discard the 100 furthest and 50 nearest points. 7. Plane Assignment: Define plane boundaries by sampling random depths uniformly between validdmax and validdmin using numplanes + 1 samples: \text{boundaries} = \text{linspace}(\text{valid\d\max}, \text{valid\d\min}, \text{num\planes} + 1) Assign each point to a plane index d{\text{position}} based on which interval its depth falls into. 8. Grouping and Memory Allocation: Group points by their 2D grid position (u, v) and plane index d{\text{position}} to form voxels in the projected space. Calculate the maximum number of points in any single group/voxel for each plane to allocate memory buffers (spliteachmax). Pseudocode: Unverified code. The code below did not pass a test run against a reference implementation, or no test fits it, so it may contain errors. import numpy as np def uniformpointcloudvoxelization(points, sidelen, numineachvoxel, K, E, w, h, validdepthnear, validdepthfar, numplanes=32): """ points: (N, 3) array of (x, y, z) K: (3, 3) intrinsic matrix E: (4, 4) extrinsic matrix (camera to world) """ # 1. Bounding Box minxyz = np.min(points, axis=0) maxxyz = np.max(points, axis=0) minx, miny, minz = minxyz maxx, maxy, maxz = maxxyz # 2. Voxel Indices numx = int(np.ceil((maxx - minx) / sidelen)) numy = int(np.ceil((maxy - miny) / sidelen)) ix = np.round((points[:, 0] - minx) / sidelen).astype(int) iy = np.round((points[:, 1] - miny) / sidelen).astype(int) iz = np.round((points[:, 2] - minz) / sidelen).astype(int) voxelindices = ix + iy numx + iz numx numy # 3. Sort by voxel index sortorder = np.argsort(voxelindices) sortedpoints = points[sortorder] sortedindices = sortorder # 4. Probabilistic Sampling uniqueindices, counts = np.unique(voxelindices[sortorder], returncounts=True) selectedmask = np.zeros(len(points), dtype=bool) currentidx = 0 for uidx, count in zip(uniqueindices, counts): endidx = currentidx + count prob = numineachvoxel / count randoms = np.random.rand(count) selectedinblock = randoms < prob selectedmask[sortedindices[currentidx:endidx][selectedinblock]] = True currentidx = endidx simplifiedpoints = points[selectedmask] # 5. Re-projection Einv = np.linalg.inv(E) homogeneouspoints = np.hstack([simplifiedpoints, np.ones((len(simplifiedpoints), 1))]) camerapoints = (Einv @ homogeneouspoints.T).T[:,:3] xc, yc, zc = camerapoints[:, 0], camerapoints[:, 1], camerapoints[:, 2] u = xc / zc v = yc / zc validdepthmask = (zc > validdepthnear) & (zc < validdepthfar) validimagemask = (u >= 0) & (u < w) & (v >= 0) & (v < h) validmask = validdepthmask & validimagemask validpoints = simplifiedpoints[validmask] validu = u[validmask] validv = v[validmask] validz = zc[validmask] # 6. Depth Filtering depthsortorder = np.argsort(-validz) sortedvalidpoints = validpoints[depthsortorder] sortedvalidu = validu[depthsortorder] sortedvalidv = validv[depthsortorder] sortedvalidz = validz[depthsortorder] if len(sortedvalidpoints) > 150: finalpoints = sortedvalidpoints[100:-50] finalu = sortedvalidu[100:-50] finalv = sortedvalidv[100:-50] finalz = sortedvalidz[100:-50] else: finalpoints = sortedvalidpoints finalu = sortedvalidu finalv = sortedvalidv finalz = sortedvalidz # 7. Plane Assignment boundaries = np.linspace(validdepthfar, validdepthnear, numplanes + 1) dpositions = np.digitize(finalz, boundaries) - 1 dpositions = np.clip(dpositions, 0, numplanes - 1) # 8. Grouping uint = np.round(finalu).astype(int) vint = np.round(finalv).astype(int) groupkeys = (dpositions (w h)) + (vint w) + uint groupsortorder = np.argsort(groupkeys) sortedgroupkeys = groupkeys[groupsortorder] sortedfinalpoints = finalpoints[groupsortorder] sortedfinalz = finalz[groupsortorder] sortedfinalu = finalu[groupsortorder] sortedfinalv = finalv[groupsortorder] uniquegroups, groupcounts = np.unique(sortedgroupkeys, returncounts=True) groupseach = np.zeros(numplanes, dtype=np.uint32) for g, c in zip(uniquegroups, groupcounts): plane = g // (w h) groupseach[plane] += c groupsindex = np.arange(len(sortedgroupkeys), dtype=np.uint32) spliteachmax = np.zeros(numplanes, dtype=np.uint16) for g, c in zip(uniquegroups, groupcounts): plane = g // (w h) if c > spliteachmax[plane]: spliteachmax[plane] = c # Compute split indices for output layout spliteachbegin = np.zeros(numplanes, dtype=np.uint32) currentoffset = 0 for plane in range(numplanes): spliteachbegin[plane] = currentoffset currentoffset += groupseach[plane] spliteachbeginingroup = np.zeros(len(uniquegroups), dtype=np.uint32) currentoffset = 0 for i, c in enumerate(groupcounts): spliteachbeginingroup[i] = currentoffset currentoffset += c groupseachindex = np.zeros(len(sortedgroupkeys), dtype=np.uint32) currentoffset = 0 for i, c in enumerate(groupcounts): groupseachindex[currentoffset:currentoffset + c] = np.arange(c, dtype=np.uint32) currentoffset += c # delta: weighting factor for aggregation. Not given in the sources. delta = np.zeros(len(sortedgroupkeys), dtype=np.float32) return { 'usorted': sortedfinalu.astype(np.uint16), 'vsorted': sortedfinalv.astype(np.uint16), 'dposition': dpositions[groupsortorder].astype(np.uint8), 'validposition': np.arange(len(sortedgroupkeys), dtype=np.uint32), 'groupseach': groupseach, 'groupsindex': groupsindex, 'groupseachindex': groupseachindex, 'spliteachbegin': spliteachbegin, 'spliteachbeginingroup': spliteachbeginingroup, 'spliteachmax': spliteachmax, 'distance': sortedfinalz.astype(np.float16), 'delta': delta } Parameters: sidelen: Voxel side length in meters. Typical values: 0.01 or 0.02. numineachvoxel: Predefined number of points to retain in each voxel after simplification. Typical values: 30 or 20. Edge Cases and Pitfalls: Empty Voxels: Voxels with no points are ignored. Precision: Depth filtering relies on float16 for distance storage, which may introduce quantization errors for very large scenes. Boundary Conditions: Points exactly on the bounding box edges or depth boundaries must be handled consistently with the rounding and clipping logic. Outlier Removal: If the total number of valid points is less than 150, the outlier removal step may discard all points. A guard should check the length before slicing. Time Complexity: Dominated by sorting points by voxel index (O(N \log N)) and sorting by depth (O(N \log N)). Probabilistic sampling is O(N). Memory Complexity: O(N) for storing point data and intermediate arrays. Output size depends on the number of non-empty voxels and points retained. Measured Performance: Not given in the sources. Strengths: Reduces point cloud density significantly while preserving structure; probabilistic sampling avoids bias towards specific points; multi-plane projection facilitates neural rendering. Limitations: Stochastic nature means results vary between runs; outlier removal may discard valid data if the cloud is sparse; requires careful tuning of sidelen and numineachvoxel. When to Use: Preprocessing for neural radiance fields (NeRF) or similar neural rendering techniques where point cloud density is too high for direct processing. When Not to Use: When deterministic voxelization is required; when exact point preservation is necessary. Originated in the context of neural rendering and point cloud processing. It was developed to handle large-scale point clouds by simplifying them before projection into multi-plane representations for efficient neural network training. https://github.com/Mayxmu/PCMP-NeRF, https://github.com/Mayxmu/PCMPNeRF, fetched 2026-10-30 (unofficial)

name: Hard Voxelization with Capacity Limits
head: Amount of Points Spawned per Voxel, Point Binning, points2voxel
body: Hard Voxelization with Capacity Limits converts a set of 3D points into a fixed-size voxel grid representation by grouping points into discrete voxels, storing their coordinates, and enforcing strict limits on the number of points per voxel and the total number of voxels. It differs from its sibling Hard Voxelization (Deterministic) by explicitly managing capacity constraints via rejection counters and chunk-based memory management, often used in scenarios requiring bounded memory usage or streaming data processing. Inputs: points: Array of 3D coordinates, shape (N, 3) or (N, 4) if labels are included. voxelsize: List of 3 floats [sx, sy, sz], defining the physical size of a single voxel in each dimension. coorsrange: List of 6 floats [x{min}, y{min}, z{min}, x{max}, y{max}, z{max}], defining the bounding box of the voxel grid. maxpoints: Integer, maximum number of points stored per voxel. Default is 35 or 5. maxvoxels: Integer, maximum number of voxels this function creates. Default is 20000. reverseindex: Boolean, whether to return coordinates in reversed order (z, y, x) instead of (x, y, z). Default is True. specificcategory: Optional list of integers, filters points by label. Points with label 31 are explicitly skipped. Outputs: voxels: Tensor of shape (M, \text{max\points}, 3) or (M, \text{max\points}, 4), containing the coordinates of points in active voxels. M is the number of active voxels. coors: Tensor of shape (M, 3), containing the voxel coordinates for each active voxel. numpointspervoxel: Tensor of shape (M), containing the count of points in each active voxel. Data Structures: coortovoxelidx: 3D array of shape (D, H, W) or (W, H, D) depending on reverseindex, initialized to -1. Maps voxel coordinates to a linear voxel index in the output arrays. voxels: Pre-allocated array of shape (\text{max\voxels}, \text{max\points}, 3), initialized to zeros. numpointspervoxel: Array of shape (\text{max\voxels}), initialized to zeros. Steps: 1. Compute Grid Shape: Calculate the dimensions of the voxel grid: \text{voxelmap\shape} = \text{tuple}\left(\text{round}\left(\frac{\text{coors\range}[3:] - \text{coors\range}[:3]}{\text{voxel\size}}\right).\text{astype}(\text{int})\right) If reverseindex is True, reverse the shape to (W, H, D). 2. Initialize Structures: Initialize coortovoxelidx with -1. Initialize numpointspervoxel with 0. Initialize voxels with 0. Set voxelnum = 0. 3. Process Points: Iterate through each point pi in points: a. Validation: If any coordinate of pi is not finite (NaN or Inf), skip the point. b. Coordinate Conversion: Compute the voxel coordinate c = (cx, cy, cz): cj = \left\lfloor \frac{p{i,j} - \text{coors\range}[j]}{\text{voxel\size}[j]} \right\rfloor \quad \text{for } j \in \{0, 1, 2\}. Alternatively, implemented as c = \lfloor p \cdot (1 / \text{resolution}) \rfloor. c. Boundary Check: If cj < 0 or cj \ge \text{voxelmap\shape}[j] for any j, skip the point. d. Label Filtering: If specificcategory is provided and the point's label is not in the list (or is 31), skip the point. e. Index Mapping: If reverseindex is True, reverse the coordinate order: c' = (cz, cy, cx). Look up voxelidx = coortovoxelidx[c']. If voxelidx == -1: If voxelnum >= maxvoxels, skip the point. Else, assign voxelidx = voxelnum, increment voxelnum, set coortovoxelidx[c'] = voxelidx, and initialize coors[voxelidx] = c'. f. Point Insertion: If numpointspervoxel[voxelidx] < maxpoints: Store pi into voxels[voxelidx, numpointspervoxel[voxelidx]]. Increment numpointspervoxel[voxelidx]. Else: Increment rejectedcount. 4. Post-Processing: Slice voxels, coors, and numpointspervoxel to voxelnum and return. Pseudocode: Unverified code. The code below did not pass a test run against a reference implementation, or no test fits it, so it may contain errors. import numpy as np import math def hardvoxelizationwithcapacitylimits(points, voxelsize, coorsrange, maxpoints=35, maxvoxels=20000, reverseindex=True, specificcategory=None): # 1. Compute grid shape voxelmapshape = tuple(round((coorsrange[i+3] - coorsrange[i]) / voxelsize[i]) for i in range(3)) if reverseindex: voxelmapshape = voxelmapshape[::-1] # 2. Initialize structures coortovoxelidx = np.full(voxelmapshape, -1, dtype=np.int32) numpointspervoxel = np.zeros(maxvoxels, dtype=np.int32) voxels = np.zeros((maxvoxels, maxpoints, points.shape[1]), dtype=points.dtype) coors = np.zeros((maxvoxels, 3), dtype=np.int32) voxelnum = 0 # 3. Process points for i in range(points.shape[0]): p = points[i] # Validation if not np.all(np.isfinite(p[:3])): continue # Coordinate conversion voxelcoord = np.floor((p[:3] - np.array(coorsrange[:3])) / np.array(voxelsize)).astype(np.int32) # Boundary check if np.any(voxelcoord < 0) or np.any(voxelcoord >= voxelmapshape): continue # Label filtering if specificcategory is not None and len(p) > 3: label = int(p[3]) if label == 31 or label not in specificcategory: continue # Index mapping coor = voxelcoord[::-1] if reverseindex else voxelcoord voxelidx = coortovoxelidx[coor[0], coor[1], coor[2]] if voxelidx == -1: if voxelnum >= maxvoxels: continue voxelidx = voxelnum voxelnum += 1 coortovoxelidx[coor[0], coor[1], coor[2]] = voxelidx coors[voxelidx] = coor # Point insertion if numpointspervoxel[voxelidx] < maxpoints: voxels[voxelidx, numpointspervoxel[voxelidx]] = p numpointspervoxel[voxelidx] += 1 else: # Rejected point pass # 4. Slice and return return voxels[:voxelnum], coors[:voxelnum], numpointspervoxel[:voxelnum] Edge Cases and Pitfalls: Points outside coorsrange are skipped. If voxelnum reaches maxvoxels, subsequent points are dropped. To ensure randomness in which points are dropped, points should be shuffled before calling. If a voxel reaches maxpoints, additional points are dropped. In streaming implementations, chunk readiness must be polled with a timeout (e.g., 10ms) to avoid infinite blocking during disk I/O. Updates voxel occupancy probabilities using raytracing hits and misses, adding confidence measures to deterministic hard voxelization. Choose when smoother integration of sparse data is needed. Time Complexity: O(N) where N is the number of points, assuming constant-time array lookup for voxel coordinates. Memory Complexity: O(\text{max\voxels} \times \text{max\points}) for the output arrays, plus O(\text{voxelmap\shape}) for the coordinate-to-index map. Performance: Performance is limited by memory bandwidth when writing to the voxels array and by cache efficiency of the coortovoxelidx map. Strengths: Bounded memory usage, deterministic output, simple implementation. Limitations: Points are dropped if capacity limits are reached, which can lead to information loss in dense regions. When to use: When memory is constrained, or when processing streaming data with known bounds. When not to use: When preserving all point information is critical, or when the point distribution is highly variable and exceeds capacity limits frequently. Hard Voxelization with Capacity Limits is used in neural rendering pipelines like VET and 3D detection frameworks like MMDetection3D, often for bounded memory voxelization. It is commonly implemented in custom voxelization libraries like voxlvoxl. name: Probabilistic Raytracing Occupancy Update
head: Occupancy Log-Odds Update, Raytraced Probability Update
body: This method updates voxel occupancy probabilities by combining direct point insertions with raytracing hits and misses, incrementing log-odds on hits and decrementing on misses, bounded by configurable thresholds. It extends deterministic hard voxelization by introducing probabilistic confidence measures for voxel occupancy, allowing smoother integration of sparse point cloud data into dense voxel grids. Inputs and Outputs: Input: A list of 3D points, a voxel grid with chunks and cells, configuration parameters (cfg), and an origin point for raytracing. Output: Updated voxel grid where cell occupancy probabilities (problog) are adjusted based on point insertions and raytracing results. Data Structures: Chunk: Contains an accessor for cell values and a state flag (MODIFIED). Cell: Contains points (array of 3D points), numpoints (count), raytraceid (integer identifier for the current raytracing pass), and problog (log-odds value representing occupancy probability). Configuration (cfg): Contains doraytracing (boolean), probhit (log-odds increment per hit), probmiss (log-odds increment per miss), occupancymaxthreshold, occupancyminthreshold, and maxpointspervoxel. Numbered Steps: 1. Point Insertion: For each point, check if all coordinates are finite; skip if not. 2. Convert the point to voxel coordinates. 3. If cfg.doraytracing is true, store the voxel coordinate in raytracehits. 4. Determine the chunk index for the voxel coordinate. 5. If the chunk is not in the neighbor window, skip the point. 6. If the cell exists and numpoints < maxpointspervoxel, add the point to the cell; otherwise, create a new cell with the point. 7. Mark the chunk as MODIFIED and increment insertion counters. 8. Raytracing Pass: If cfg.doraytracing is true, define a clear callback for the ray iterator: for each coordinate along the ray, if the chunk is in the neighbor window and the cell exists with raytraceid != raytraceiterid, set raytraceid = raytraceiterid, update problog = max(problog + probmiss, occupancyminthreshold), and mark the chunk MODIFIED; if the cell does not exist, skip it to avoid memory bloat. 9. Iterate through raytracehits: for each target coordinate to, raytrace from the origin to to using a RayIterator, invoking the clear callback for every cell along the path (misses). 10. After the raytrace, update the target cell at to directly: if it exists and raytraceid != raytraceiterid, set raytraceid = raytraceiterid, update problog = min(problog + probhit, occupancymaxthreshold), and mark the chunk MODIFIED. 11. Clear raytracehits and increment raytraceiterid after processing all hits. Formulas: For hits: prob\log{new} = \min(prob\log{old} + prob\hit, occupancy\max\threshold). For misses: prob\log{new} = \max(prob\log{old} + prob\miss, occupancy\min\threshold). Parameters: probmiss: Log-odds increment per ray miss (decreases probability); value not specified in the code. probhit: Log-odds increment per ray hit; value not specified in the code. occupancymaxthreshold: Maximum problog value; value not specified in the code. occupancyminthreshold: Minimum problog value; value not specified in the code. Edge Cases and Pitfalls: Redundant Updates: raytraceiterid prevents redundant updates within the same raytracing pass; cells must be checked against it before updating. Missing Cells: The RayIterator callback must handle missing cells gracefully; the code logs an error but does not create cells to avoid memory bloat. Precision: Log-odds values can become very large or small; thresholds should be set appropriately to prevent overflow or underflow. Boundary Conditions: Points outside the neighbor window are ignored; the window size must be sufficient to capture relevant data. Pseudocode: Unverified code. The code below did not pass a test run against a reference implementation, or no test fits it, so it may contain errors. import math from dataclasses import dataclass from typing import List, Tuple, Dict, Any @dataclass class Coord: x: int y: int z: int @dataclass class Cell: points: List[Tuple[float, float, float]] numpoints: int raytraceid: int problog: float @dataclass class Chunk: class State: MODIFIED = 1 state: int accessor: Dict[Coord, Cell] def updateoccupancy(points: List[Tuple[float, float, float]], origin: Tuple[float, float, float], cfg: Dict[str, Any], chunkmap: Dict[Coord, Chunk], currentsourcechunkidx: Coord, raytracehits: List[Coord], raytraceiterid: List[int], cellsize: float = 1.0, chunksize: int = 16) -> Tuple[int, int, int]: insertcount = 0 outofrangecount = 0 rejectedcount = 0 for p in points: if not (math.isfinite(p[0]) and math.isfinite(p[1]) and math.isfinite(p[2])): continue voxelcoord = Coord(int(p[0] / cellsize), int(p[1] / cellsize), int(p[2] / cellsize)) if cfg["doraytracing"]: raytracehits.append(voxelcoord) pointchunkidx = Coord(voxelcoord.x // chunksize, voxelcoord.y // chunksize, voxelcoord.z // chunksize) if not (abs(pointchunkidx.x - name: Probabilistic Voxel Representation
head: OpenVox, OpenVox Probabilistic Voxel Representation
body: Probabilistic Voxel Representation is a real-time, instance-level open-vocabulary mapping method that enhances robustness in incremental 3D reconstruction by modeling voxel occupancy and semantic identity through probabilistic distributions. Unlike deterministic hard-voxel approaches that suffer from compounding errors due to segmentation inaccuracies, this method uses Maximum Likelihood Estimation (MLE) for instance association and Maximum A Posteriori (MAP) estimation for map evolution, allowing it to handle under-segmentation and poor viewing angles gracefully. It builds on Probabilistic Raytracing Occupancy Update by extending probabilistic modeling from binary occupancy to multi-instance semantic vectors and codebook features. The method operates in a loop of Instance Association and Live Map Evolution for each incoming frame observation Qt = \{ \{m{ti}, f{ti}\}, Dt, Pt \}, where m{ti} is a 2D instance mask, f{ti} is its feature embedding, Dt is the depth image, and Pt is the camera pose. Inputs: Current frame masks \{m{ti}\}, mask features \{f{ti}\}, depth map Dt, camera pose Pt, camera intrinsics K, and existing map M{t-1} = \{V{t-1}, B{t-1}\}. Outputs: Updated map Mt = \{Vt, Bt\} and instance assignments It. 1. Voxel Map V: A 3D grid with resolution 0.04\text{m}. Each voxel vj stores a probabilistic instance ID vector \thetaj = \{ \theta{j,\gamma} \mid \gamma \in \Gamma \}, where \Gamma is the set of known instance IDs. \theta{j,\gamma} > 0 and \sum{\gamma \in \Gamma} \theta{j,\gamma} = 1. \theta{j,\gamma} represents the probability that voxel vj belongs to instance \gamma. 2. Embedding Codebook B: Associates each instance ID \gamma with a fused caption feature vector f\gamma and a cumulative weight W\gamma. Voxel Resolution: 0.04\text{m}. Similarity Threshold: Fixed threshold for association validity (exact value not specified in sources). Prior Probability: Assumed uniform across all existing instances \Gamma{t-1} for MLE. 1. Voxel Region Projection: For each mask m{ti} with pixel coordinates [u, v], project the mask into the voxel map using depth Dt and camera intrinsics K: V{m{ti}} = \text{Vox}( Dt[u,v] \cdot Pt \cdot K^{-1} \cdot [u, v]^T \mid [u, v] \in m{ti}) where \text{Vox}(\cdot) transforms 3D points to voxel indices. 2. Instance Association: Unobserved Region: If V{m{ti}} contains no voxels with existing instance information, add a new instance ID \gamma{new} to \Gamma{t-1} and initialize its embedding in B{t-1} using f{ti}. Observed Region: If V{m{ti}} contains voxels with instance information, determine the best matching existing instance \gamma \in \Gamma{t-1}: 1. Geometric Similarity (SI{geo}): Compute the average likelihood probability of the voxels in V{m{ti}} for instance \gamma. To avoid numerical underflow from multiplying probabilities, use the law of large numbers by averaging: SI{geo}^{i=\gamma} = \mathbb{E}(\{ \theta{mi}^j [\gamma] \}) = \frac{1}{|V{m{ti}}|} \sum{vj \in V{m{ti}}} \theta{j,\gamma} where \theta{j,\gamma} is the probability of voxel vj belonging to instance \gamma from the previous map. 2. Feature Similarity (SI{fea}): Compute the cosine similarity between the mask feature f{ti} and the codebook feature f\gamma of instance \gamma. 3. Association Probability (A): Fuse the similarities via weighted fusion (specific weights not provided in sources). 4. Decision: If \max{\gamma} (A{I{ti}=\gamma}) exceeds the similarity threshold, associate m{ti} with the corresponding instance ID I{ti}. Otherwise, initialize a new instance. 3. Live Map Evolution (Voxel Update): Update the probabilistic instance vector \thetaj for each voxel vj \in V{m{ti}} using MAP estimation with a Dirichlet conjugate prior. Let \alpha{t-1, j, \gamma} be the prior parameter for voxel vj and instance \gamma. Let y{tj, \gamma} be a one-hot encoded measurement tuple indicating the association of the current frame's instance I{ti} to instance \gamma (i.e., y{tj, I{ti}} = 1, others 0). Update the parameter \alpha: \alpha{t, j, \gamma} = \alpha{t-1, j, \gamma} + y{tj, \gamma} Compute the new probabilistic instance vector \theta{t, j} as the expected value of the posterior Dirichlet distribution: \theta{t, j, \gamma} = \frac{\alpha{t, j, \gamma}}{\sum{\tau \in \Gamma} \alpha{t, j, \tau}} This model is referred to as the "instance counting sensor model". 4. Live Map Evolution (Codebook Update): Update the embedding codebook B for the associated instance I{ti}. Visibility Ratio (R{ti}): Calculate the proportion of the instance's size observed by the current mask relative to the total instance size. This prevents contamination from poor viewing angles (e.g., only a corner visible). Credibility Weight (w{ti}): w{ti} = A{I{ti}} \cdot R{ti} where A{I{ti}} is the association probability for the chosen instance. Weight Update: W{t}^{I{ti}} = W{t-1}^{I{ti}} + w{ti} Feature Update: f{t}^{I{ti}} = \frac{W{t-1}^{I{ti}} f{t-1}^{I{ti}} + w{ti} f{ti}}{W{t}^{I{ti}}} For instances not associated with the current mask, W and f remain unchanged. Unverified code. The code below did not pass a test run against a reference implementation, or no test fits it, so it may contain errors. import math from typing import List, Dict, Tuple, Set, Any def probabilisticvoxelrepresentationstep( framemasks: List[List[Tuple[int, int]]], framefeatures: List[List[float]], depthmap: List[List[float]], camerapose: List[List[float]], cameraintrinsics: List[List[float]], existingmap: Tuple[List[Dict[str, float]], Dict[str, Tuple[List[float], float]], Set[str], Dict[Tuple[int, str], float]], resolution: float = 0.04, similaritythreshold: float = 0.5) -> Tuple[List[Dict[str, float]], Dict[str, Tuple[List[float], float]], Set[str], Dict[Tuple[int, str], float]]: """ Performs one step of probabilistic voxel mapping. Args: framemasks: List of 2D masks, each mask is a list of (u, v) pixel coordinates. framefeatures: List of feature vectors fti corresponding to masks. depthmap: Depth image Dt as 2D list. camerapose: Camera pose Pt as 4x4 matrix. cameraintrinsics: Camera intrinsics K as 3x3 matrix. existingmap: Tuple (V, B, Gamma, alpha) V: List of voxels, each voxel is a dict mapping instanceid -> theta probability. B: Dict mapping instanceid -> (featurevector, weight). Gamma: Set of existing instance IDs. alpha: Dict mapping (voxelidx, instanceid) -> alphaparam. resolution: Voxel grid resolution in meters. similaritythreshold: Threshold for association decision. Returns: updatedmap: Tuple (V, B, Gamma, alpha) """ V, B, Gamma, alpha = existingmap # Deep copy structures to avoid in-place mutation during read newV = [dict(v) for v in V] newB = {k: (list(f), w) for k, (f, w) in B.items()} newGamma = set(Gamma) newalpha = dict(alpha) for i, (mask, feature) in enumerate(zip(framemasks, framefeatures)): # 1. Project mask to voxel region voxelindicesinmask = [] for u, v in mask: d = depthmap[v][u] if d is None or d <= 0: continue point3d = projectpixeltoworld(u, v, d, cameraintrinsics, camerapose) voxelidx = voxelizepoint(point3d, resolution) voxelindicesinmask.append(voxelidx) if not voxelindicesinmask: continue # 2. Instance Association isunobserved = True for vidx in voxelindicesinmask: if vidx < len(newV) and any(g in newV[vidx] for g in Gamma): isunobserved = False break if isunobserved: newinstanceid = f"instance{len(newGamma)}" newGamma.add(newinstanceid) newB[newinstanceid] = (list(feature), 0.0) associatedinstanceid = newinstanceid else: bestgamma = None bestscore = -1.0 for gamma in Gamma: # Geometric Similarity geosim = 0.0 count = 0 for vidx in voxelindicesinmask: if vidx < len(newV) and gamma in newV[vidx]: geosim += newV[vidx][gamma] count += 1 geosim = geosim / count if count > 0 else 0.0 # Feature Similarity if gamma in newB: featsim = cosinesimilarity(feature, newB[gamma][0]) else: featsim = 0.0 # Association Probability (Weighted Fusion) # Source mentions weighted fusion but does not specify weights score = 0.5 geosim + 0.5 featsim if score > bestscore: bestscore = score bestgamma = gamma if bestscore > similaritythreshold: associatedinstanceid = bestgamma else: newinstanceid = f"instance{len(newGamma)}" newGamma.add(newinstanceid) newB[newinstanceid] = (list(feature), 0.0) associatedinstanceid = newinstanceid # 3. Live Map Evolution: Voxel Update for vidx in voxelindicesinmask: if vidx >= len(newV): continue # Initialize alpha for new instances if needed for gamma in newGamma: key = (vidx, gamma) if key not in newalpha: newalpha[key] = 0.0 # Update alpha with one-hot measurement ytj for gamma in newGamma: key = (vidx, gamma) ytjgamma = 1.0 if gamma == associatedinstanceid else 0.0 newalpha[key] = newalpha[key] + ytjgamma # Recompute theta for this voxel totalalpha = sum(newalpha.get((vidx, g), 0.0) for g in newGamma) if totalalpha > 0: for gamma in newGamma: key = (vidx, gamma) newV[vidx][gamma] = newalpha[key] / totalalpha else: uniformprob = 1.0 / len(newGamma) if newGamma else 0.0 for gamma in newGamma: newV[vidx][gamma] = uniformprob # 4. Live Map Evolution: Codebook Update if associatedinstanceid in newB: # Visibility Ratio Rti # Source: proportion of instance's size observed. Implementation detail not specified Rti = estimatevisibilityratio(associatedinstanceid, voxelindicesinmask, newV) # Credibility weight wti wti = bestscore Rti # Update Weight currentfeat, currentweight = newB[associatedinstanceid] newweight = currentweight + wti # Update Feature newfeat = [(currentweight currentfeat[k] + wti feature[k]) / newweight for k in range(len(currentfeat))] newB[associatedinstanceid] = (newfeat, newweight) return (newV, newB, newGamma, newalpha) def projectpixeltoworld(u: int, v: int, depth: float, K: List[List[float]], P: List[List[float]]) -> List[float]: # Standard pinhole projection inverse fx, fy = K[0][0], K[1][1] cx, cy = K[0][2], K[1][2] xcam = (u - cx) / fx depth ycam = (v - cy) / fy depth zcam = depth Xcam = [xcam, ycam, zcam, 1.0] Xworld = [sum(P[r][c] Xcam[c] for c in range(4)) for r in range(4)] return Xworld[:3] def voxelizepoint(point: List[float], resolution: float) -> int: # Simple linear hashing for voxel index return int((point[0] / resolution) + (point[1] / resolution) 1000 + (point[2] / resolution) 1000000) def cosinesimilarity(v1: List[float], v2: List[float]) -> float: dot = sum(a b for a, b in zip(v1, v2)) norm1 = math.sqrt(sum(a a for a in v1)) norm2 = math.sqrt(sum(b b for b in v2)) return dot / (norm1 norm2) if norm1 > 0 and norm2 > 0 else 0.0 def estimatevisibilityratio(instanceid: str, voxelindicesinmask: List[int], V: List[Dict[str, float]]) -> float: # Placeholder for visibility ratio calculation as exact method not provided in sources # Returns a value between 0 and 1 return 1.0 Numerical Underflow: Multiplying likelihood probabilities of independent voxels causes underflow. Mitigated by averaging likelihood probabilities (geometric similarity). Poor Viewing Contamination: Features from partial views (e.g., only a corner visible) can corrupt the global codebook. Mitigated by weighting updates with the visibility ratio R{ti}. Inaccurate Segmentation: If the front-end segmentation is inaccurate or under-segmented, deterministic methods fail. Probabilistic modeling provides robustness by allowing soft associations. Time Complexity: Depends on the number of voxels in the mask region and the number of instances in \Gamma. The MLE step iterates over all instances for each mask, and the voxel update iterates over all voxels in the mask region. Real-time performance is claimed on an RTX 4090. Memory Complexity: Proportional to the number of voxels times the number of instances (for \theta vectors) plus the size of the codebook. The voxel resolution of 0.04\text{m} balances precision and memory. Strengths: Robust to segmentation errors, handles open-vocabulary semantics via LLM captions, real-time capable. Limitations: Requires accurate depth and camera poses. Performance degrades if visibility ratio estimation is poor. When to use: Incremental mapping where robustness to segmentation errors is critical, and open-vocabulary semantic understanding is required. When not to use: Resource-constrained environments where memory for large instance vectors is prohibitive, or when high-precision geometric reconstruction is prioritized over semantic robustness. Probabilistic Voxel Representation, as implemented in OpenVox, addresses limitations of previous incremental mapping methods like ConceptGraphs, which are prone to compounding errors from inaccurate segmentation. The method leverages probabilistic modeling (Dirichlet priors) for instance association and fusion, inspired by semantic counting sensor models. It is implemented in PyTorch and tested on robotics platforms. name: Vectorized Voxelization
head: Vectorized Point Cloud Voxelization
body: Vectorized Voxelization is a vectorized algorithm that bins 3D points into a voxel grid, averaging colors per cell, and returns voxel centers, averaged colors, and the grid origin. It sets itself apart from sibling methods by using a fully vectorized NumPy pipeline with cumulative-sum aggregation and row-major key flattening, avoiding explicit loops or GPU-specific sort-scatter kernels. Inputs: positions: Array of shape (N, 3), dtype float32, representing 3D coordinates of N points. colors: Optional array of shape (N, 3), dtype uint8 (0–255). If None, a grayscale height map is generated. opacities: Optional array of shape (N,), dtype float32. resolution: Float, the side length of each voxel cube. origin: Optional array of shape (3,), dtype float32. If None, computed as positions.min(axis=0). minopacity: Float, default 0.0. Points with opacity below this are discarded. densitythreshold: Int, default 1. Voxels with fewer points than this are discarded. Outputs: centers: Array of shape (M, 3), dtype float32, representing the 3D coordinates of the M active voxel centers. colors: Array of shape (M, 3), dtype float32, representing the averaged colors in the range [0, 1]. origin: Array of shape (3,), dtype float32, the grid origin used for quantization. Data Structures: grid: Array of shape (N, 3), dtype int64, storing the integer voxel indices for each point. keys: Array of shape (N,), dtype int64, storing the flattened 1D index for each voxel. uniquekeys: Array of shape (K,), dtype int64, storing the sorted, unique voxel keys. counts: Array of shape (K,), dtype int64, storing the number of points per unique voxel. Steps: 1. Opacity Filtering: If opacities is provided and minopacity > 0.0, filter positions, colors, and opacities to keep only indices where opacities >= minopacity. 2. Fallback Color Generation: If colors is None, compute a grayscale color based on the height (z-coordinate) of the points: z = \text{positions}[:, 2] t = \frac{z - \min(z)}{\max(\text{ptp}(z), 10^{-8})} \text{colors} = \text{repeat}\left( \left( t \times 255 \right).astype(\text{uint8}), 3, \text{axis}=1 \right) where \text{ptp}(z) = \max(z) - \min(z). 3. Origin Initialization: If origin is None, set origin = positions.min(axis=0) and cast origin to np.float32. 4. Quantization: Compute the integer grid coordinates for each point: \text{grid} = \left\lfloor \frac{\text{positions} - \text{origin}}{\text{resolution}} \right\rfloor.astype(\text{int64}). 5. Non-Negative Shift: Ensure all grid indices are non-negative for hashing: \text{grid\offset} = \text{grid.min(axis=0)} \text{grid} \leftarrow \text{grid} - \text{grid\offset}. 6. Grid Dimensions: Compute the dimensions of the bounding box in voxels: \text{dims} = \text{grid.max(axis=0)} + 1. 7. Flattening: Collapse 3D indices (gx, gy, gz) into a single 1D key using row-major ordering: \text{keys} = (\text{grid}[:, 0] \times \text{dims}[1] + \text{grid}[:, 1]) \times \text{dims}[2] + \text{grid}[:, 2]. 8. Sorting: Sort the keys to group identical voxels together: \text{order} = \text{argsort}(\text{keys}) \text{keys\sorted} = \text{keys}[\text{order}]. 9. Unique Identification: Find unique voxel keys and their first occurrence indices and counts: \text{unique\keys}, \text{start}, \text{counts} = \text{unique}(\text{keys\sorted}, \text{return\index}=\text{True}, \text{return\counts}=\text{True}). 10. Color Aggregation: Compute the sum of colors for each unique voxel using cumulative sums on the sorted colors: \text{colors\sorted} = \text{colors}[\text{order}] \text{csum} = \text{cumsum}(\text{colors\sorted.astype}(\text{float64}), \text{axis}=0) Prepend a zero row to csum: \text{csum} = \text{vstack}([\text{zeros}(3), \text{csum}]) Compute sums at the boundaries of each unique group: \text{color\sums} = \text{csum}[\text{start} + \text{counts}] - \text{csum}[\text{start}]. 11. Averaging: Compute the average color per voxel and normalize to [0, 1]: \text{avg\colors} = \left( \frac{\text{color\sums}}{\text{counts}[:, \text{None}]} \right).astype(\text{float32}) / 255.0. 12. Density Filtering: If densitythreshold > 1, filter out voxels with insufficient points: \text{keep} = \text{counts} \ge \text{density\threshold} \text{unique\keys} \leftarrow \text{unique\keys}[\text{keep}] \text{avg\colors} \leftarrow \text{avg\colors}[\text{keep}]. 13. Center Reconstruction: Reconstruct the 3D coordinates of the voxel centers from the flattened keys: gz = \text{unique\keys} \% \text{dims}[2] gy = (\text{unique\keys} // \text{dims}[2]) \% \text{dims}[1] gx = \text{unique\keys} // (\text{dims}[1] \times \text{dims}[2]) \text{centers} = \text{origin} + (\text{stack}([gx, gy, gz]).T + 0.5) \times \text{resolution} The standard interpretation for voxel centers is the grid index plus 0.5, scaled by resolution, added to the origin. Parameters: resolution: Float, the side length of each voxel cube. minopacity: Float, default 0.0; points with opacity below this threshold are discarded before voxelization. densitythreshold: Int, default 1; voxels with fewer points than this value are discarded. origin: np.ndarray or None, default None; the grid origin for quantization. If None, defaults to the minimum corner of the point cloud positions. Edge Cases and Pitfalls: If all points are removed by the opacity filter, the algorithm must raise ValueError: 'Every point was removed by the opacity filter - lower Min opacity'. Division by zero in the fallback color generation is guarded by max(float(np.ptp(z)), 1e-8). Negative grid coordinates are handled by the non-negative shift step to ensure valid array indexing and key flattening. Pseudocode: Unverified code. The code below did not pass a test run against a reference implementation, or no test fits it, so it may contain errors. import numpy as np def vectorizedvoxelization(positions, colors=None, opacities=None, resolution=0.05, origin=None, minopacity=0.0, densitythreshold=1): """ Vectorized voxelization of a point cloud. Args: positions: (N, 3) float32 array of point coordinates. colors: (N, 3) uint8 array (0-255) or None. opacities: (N,) float32 array or None. resolution: float, voxel side length. origin: (3,) float32 array or None. minopacity: float, minimum opacity threshold. densitythreshold: int, minimum points per voxel. Returns: centers: (M, 3) float32 array of voxel centers. colors: (M, 3) float32 array of averaged colors (0-1). origin: (3,) float32 array of grid origin. """ # 1. Opacity Filtering if opacities is not None and minopacity > 0.0: mask = opacities >= minopacity if not np.any(mask): raise ValueError('Every point was removed by the opacity filter - lower Min opacity') positions = positions[mask] if colors is not None: colors = colors[mask] opacities = opacities[mask] # 2. Fallback Color Generation if colors is None: z = positions[:, 2] zrange = max(float(np.ptp(z)), 1e-8) t = (z - np.min(z)) / zrange colors = np.repeat((t[:, None] 255).astype(np.uint8), 3, axis=1) # 3. Origin Initialization if origin is None: origin = np.min(positions, axis=0).astype(np.float32) else: origin = origin.astype(np.float32) # 4. Quantization grid = np.floor((positions - origin) / resolution).astype(np.int64) # 5. Non-Negative Shift gridoffset = np.min(grid, axis=0) grid -= gridoffset # 6. Grid Dimensions dims = np.max(grid, axis=0) + 1 # 7. Flattening keys = (grid[:, 0] dims[1] + grid[:, 1]) dims[2] + grid[:, 2] # 8. Sorting order = np.argsort(keys) keyssorted = keys[order] # 9. Unique Identification uniquekeys, start, counts = np.unique(keyssorted, returnindex=True, returncounts=True) # 10. Color Aggregation colorssorted = colors[order].astype(np.float64) csum = np.cumsum(colorssorted, axis=0) csum = np.vstack([np.zeros(3), csum]) colorsums = csum[start + counts] - csum[start] # 11. Averaging avgcolors = (colorsums / counts[:, None]).astype(np.float32) / 255.0 # 12. Density Filtering if densitythreshold > 1: keep = counts >= densitythreshold uniquekeys = uniquekeys[keep] avgcolors = avgcolors[keep] # 13. Center Reconstruction gz = uniquekeys % dims[2] gy = (uniquekeys // dims[2]) % dims[1] gx = uniquekeys // (dims[1] dims[2]) centers = origin + (np.stack([gx, gy, gz], axis=-1).astype(np.float32) + 0.5) resolution return centers, avgcolors, origin Time complexity: Not given in the sources. Memory complexity: Not given in the sources. Performance: Not given in the sources. Strengths: Not given in the sources. Limitations: Not given in the sources. name: Point Cloud Voxelization with Adjacency Cleanup
head: Open3DUE5Module::VoxelizedArrFromPoints with Cleanup, Point Cloud 3D Reconstruction with DEFTET
body: This method converts a set of 3D points into a fixed-size voxel grid by assigning each point to a discrete voxel based on its coordinates and a specified voxel size, then removes isolated, non-connected voxels to clean up noise. It builds on Hard Voxelization (Deterministic) by adding a topological cleanup phase. Inputs: Points: Array of 3D coordinates. Transform: Transformation matrix applied to points. bSubtractive: Boolean flag; if true, inverts Settings.DistanceDivisor by multiplying it by -1 to handle subtractive voxelization. Settings: Configuration object containing VoxelSize (double/float) and DistanceDivisor. Outputs: Asset: A voxel data asset containing the final grid, position offset, and subtractive flag. Return value: Boolean indicating success or failure. Data Structures: Data: 3D array (grid) accessed via SetValue(X, Y, Z, value) and GetValue(X, Y, Z, value), with size managed by SetSize(FIntVector, bool). FVoxelValue: Enum with states Empty(), Full(), and Special(). VoxelFilledArr: Array of integer coordinates (X, Y, Z) representing occupied voxels returned by the core voxelization module. RealSize: 3D integer vector defining the dimensions of the output grid. OutOffset: 3D integer vector representing the minimum coordinate offset of the grid in world space. Steps: 1. Validation: If Points is empty, return false. 2. Subtractive Adjustment: If bSubtractive is true, multiply Settings.DistanceDivisor by -1. 3. name: Voxel Hashing with Mean Aggregation
head: BEVFusion Voxelization, Hard Voxelization (Deterministic) with Feature Aggregation, Hash Voxelization, Hash-based Point Cloud Voxelization, Hash-based Voxelization, Scatter Mean Voxelization, Voxel Hashing and Mean Aggregation
body:
A GPU-accelerated voxelization pipeline for LiDAR point clouds that converts 3D points into a fixed-size voxel grid using a hash table for coordinate mapping, scatter operations for feature accumulation, and a reducemean kernel for feature aggregation. It sets itself apart from sibling methods by using open-addressing hash tables with linear probing to handle collisions and deduplicate points within the same voxel, followed by a two-pass feature reduction (scatter then mean) rather than simple max-pooling or fixed-array accumulation. Inputs: points: Array of shape (N, F), where N is the number of points and F is the number of features per point (e.g., x, y, z, intensity). Data type: half (16-bit float). param: Configuration object containing: minrange: 3D vector (min\x, min\y, min\z) defining the minimum bounds of the voxel grid in world coordinates. maxrange: 3D vector (max\x, max\y, max\z) defining the maximum bounds. voxelsize: 3D vector (v\x, v\y, v\z) defining the physical size of each voxel. gridsize: 3D integer vector (G\x, G\y, G\z), computed as \lceil (maxange - minange) / voxel\size ceil. maxvoxels: Maximum number of voxels allowed in the output. maxpointspervoxel: Maximum number of points stored per voxel. numfeature: Number of features per point F. CoordinateOrder: Enum, either XYZ or ZYX, determining the storage order of voxel indices. Outputs: dvoxelfeatures: Array of shape (M, F), where M is the number of valid voxels created. Data type: half. dvoxelindices: Array of shape (M, 4). Each element is a 4-tuple. For XYZ order: \{0, x, y, z\}. For ZYX order: \{0, z, y, x\}, where x, y, z are the voxel coordinates. drealnumvoxels: Scalar, the total number of voxels created. Data Structures: 1. hashtable: Array of uint32t of size H = N 	imes 8. The first half (0 to H/2 - 1) stores voxel offsets (keys). The second half (H/2 to H - 1) stores corresponding voxel IDs (values). Initialized to UINT32MAX (0xff) for keys. 2. voxelstemp: Array of float of size max\voxels 	imes max\points\per\voxel 	imes num eature. Layout: [voxelid][pointidx][featureidx]. Stores temporary float features before reduction. 3. numpointspervoxel: Array of uint32t of size max\voxels. Stores the count of points currently in each voxel. 4. voxelindices: Array of uint32t of size max\voxels 	imes 4. Stores voxel coordinates as uint4. Hash Function: The hash function maps a 32-bit integer key k to a 32-bit hash value:  egin{aligned} k &= k \oplus (k \gg 16) \ k &= k 	imes 0x85ebca6b \ k &= k \oplus (k \gg 13) \ k &= k 	imes 0xc2b2ae35 \ k &= k \oplus (k \gg 16) \ 	ext{return } k \end{aligned} Steps: 1. Initialization: Allocate device memory for hashtable, voxelstemp, dvoxelfeatures, dvoxelnum, dvoxelindices, drealnumvoxels, and hrealnumvoxels. Reset hashtable keys to UINT32MAX and numpointspervoxel to 0 using memset. 2. Build Hash Table (Kernel 1): Launch a kernel with one thread per point (N threads). For each point i, extract coordinates (px, py, pz) from points[i]. Compute voxel indices:  egin{aligned} voxel\idx &= \lfloor (px - minange.x) / voxel\size.x floor \ voxel\idy &= \lfloor (py - minange.y) / voxel\size.y floor \ voxel\idz &= \lfloor (pz - minange.z) / voxel\size.z floor \end{aligned} Boundary Check: If any index is < 0 or \ge corresponding gridsize dimension, discard the point. Compute linear voxel offset: voxel\offset = (voxel\idz 	imes grid\size.y + voxel\idy) 	imes grid\size.x + voxel\idx Hash Table Insertion: Calculate slot: slot = hash(voxel\offset) \% (H / 2). Use open addressing with linear probing: Load key k from hashtable[slot]. If k == voxel\offset: Key exists. Break (point is a duplicate in this voxel). If k == UINT32\MAX: Slot is empty. Atomically increment realvoxelnum to get a new unique voxelid. Atomically store voxeloffset in hashtable[slot] and voxelid in hashtable[slot + H/2]. Else: Probe next slot: slot = (slot + 1) \% (H / 2). 3. Voxelization and Feature Scattering (Kernel 2): Launch a kernel with one thread per point (N threads). For each point i, compute voxeloffset and voxelid as in Step 2. Lookup: Call lookuphashtable(voxeloffset, H, hashtable). If result is UINT32MAX or \ge max\voxels, discard point. Atomic Count: Atomically increment numpointspervoxel[voxelid]. Let currentnum be the returned value. Feature Storage: If currentnum < maxpointspervoxel: Calculate destination offset in voxelstemp: dst\offset = voxel\id 	imes (num eature 	imes max\points\per\voxel) + current
um 	imes num eature Copy features from points[i] to voxelstemp[dstoffset: dstoffset + numfeature]. Write voxel coordinates to voxelindices[voxelid] based on CoordinateOrder (e.g., {0, x, y, z} for XYZ). 4. Reduce Mean (Kernel 3): Launch a kernel with one thread per possible voxel (max\voxels threads). For each voxel j: Read validpointsnum = numpointspervoxel[j]. Clamp validpointsnum to maxpointspervoxel. If validpointsnum <= 0, skip (avoid division by zero). Initialize accumulator array acc of size numfeature to 0. Sum features: acc[f] = \sum{p=0}^{valid\points
um - 1} voxels	emp[j 	imes max\points\per\voxel 	imes num eature + p 	imes num eature + f] for f \in [0, num eature). Compute mean: d\voxel eatures[j 	imes num eature + f] = (sycl::half)(acc[f] / valid\points
um) 5. Finalization: Asynchronously copy drealnumvoxels to host hrealnumvoxels. The output dvoxelfeatures contains the aggregated voxel features in half-precision. Pseudocode: Unverified code. The code below did not pass a test run against a reference implementation, or no test fits it, so it may contain errors. def voxelhashingmeanaggregation(points, param): N = points.shape[0] F = param.numfeature H = N 8 # Hash table size maxvoxels = param.maxvoxels maxppv = param.maxpointspervoxel # 1. Initialization hashtable = arrayuint32(H, fill=UINT32MAX) numpointspervoxel = arrayuint32(maxvoxels, fill=0) voxelstemp = arrayfloat(maxvoxels maxppv F, fill=0.0) # Stale data safe voxelindices = arrayuint32(maxvoxels 4, fill=0) realvoxelnum = 0 # 2. Build Hash Table Kernel # Launch N threads for i in range(N): px, py, pz = points[i, 0], points[i, 1], points[i, 2] # Voxel Index Calculation voxelidx = floor((px - param.minrange.x) / param.voxelsize.x) voxelidy = floor((py - param.minrange.y) / param.voxelsize.y) voxelidz = floor((pz - param.minrange.z) / param.voxelsize.z) # Boundary Check if not (0 <= voxelidx < param.gridsize.x and 0 <= voxelidy < param.gridsize.y and 0 <= voxelidz < param.gridsize.z): continue voxeloffset = (voxelidz param.gridsize.y + voxelidy) param.gridsize.x + voxelidx # Hash Table Insertion slot = hash(voxeloffset) % (H // 2) while True: k = atomicload(hashtable, slot) if k == voxeloffset: break # Duplicate elif k == UINT32MAX: # Empty slot, assign new voxel ID voxelid = atomicadd(realvoxelnum, 1) atomicstore(hashtable, slot, voxeloffset) atomicstore(hashtable, slot + H // 2, voxelid) break else: slot = (slot + 1) % (H // 2) # Linear probing # 3. Voxelization and Feature Scattering Kernel # Launch N threads for i in range(N): px, py, pz = points[i, 0], points[i, 1], points[i, 2] # Recompute voxeloffset (or cache it) voxelidx = floor((px - param.minrange.x) / param.voxelsize.x) voxelidy = floor((py - param.minrange.y) / param.voxelsize.y) voxelidz = floor((pz - param.minrange.z) / param.voxelsize.z) voxeloffset = (voxelidz param.gridsize.y + voxelidy) param.gridsize.x + voxelidx # Lookup voxelid = lookuphashtable(voxeloffset, H, hashtable) if voxelid == UINT32MAX or voxelid >= param.maxvoxels: continue # Atomic Count currentnum = atomicadd(numpointspervoxel, voxelid, 1) if currentnum < maxppv: dstoffset = voxelid (F maxppv) + currentnum F srcoffset = i F for f in range(F): voxelstemp[dstoffset + f] = float(points[i, f]) # Save indices if param.CoordinateOrder == XYZ: voxelindices[voxelid 4: voxelid 4 + 4] = [0, voxelidx, voxelidy, voxelidz] else: # ZYX voxelindices[voxelid 4: voxelid 4 + 4] = [0, voxelidz, voxelidy, voxelidx] # 4. Reduce Mean Kernel # Launch maxvoxels threads dvoxelfeatures = arrayhalf(maxvoxels F) for j in range(maxvoxels): validpointsnum = numpointspervoxel[j] if validpointsnum > maxppv: validpointsnum = maxppv if validpointsnum <= 0: continue acc = [0.0] F offset = j maxppv F for p in range(validpointsnum): ptoffset = offset + p F for f in range(F): acc[f] += voxelstemp[ptoffset + f] inv = 1.0 / validpointsnum for f in range(F): dvoxelfeatures[j F + f] = half(acc[f] inv) return dvoxelfeatures, voxelindices, realvoxelnum def hash(k): k = k ^ (k >> 16) k = k 0x85ebca6b k = k ^ (k >> 13) k = k 0xc2b2ae35 k = k ^ (k >> 16) return k def lookuphashtable(key, hashsize, hashtable): slot = hash(key) % (hashsize // 2) while True: k = atomicload(hashtable, slot) if k == key: return atomicload(hashtable, slot + hashsize // 2) elif k == UINT32MAX: return UINT32MAX else: slot = (slot + 1) % (hashsize // 2) return UINT32MAX Time Complexity: O(N) for hash table construction and scattering, O(M 	imes max\points\per\voxel 	imes F) for reduction, where N is points, M is voxels, F is features. Memory Complexity: O(N) for hash table, O(M 	imes max\points\per\voxel 	imes F) for temporary storage. Performance: The method is optimized for GPU execution using atomic operations and coalesced memory access patterns. The use of half precision for output reduces memory bandwidth. Strengths: Handles variable point density efficiently; deterministic output; supports feature aggregation beyond simple coordinates. Limitations: Hash table collisions can lead to probing overhead; load factor is kept low (0.25) to minimize collisions, increasing memory usage. When to use: LiDAR point cloud processing for autonomous driving (e.g., BEVFusion, CenterPoint) where deterministic voxelization with feature aggregation is required. When not to use: When memory is extremely constrained (due to hash table size) or when non-deterministic aggregation is acceptable (e.g., max pooling). Originated from NVIDIA's LidarAISolution CUDA-BEVFusion implementation. It has been ported to SYCL for Intel GPUs. The method is widely used in 3D object detection pipelines for autonomous vehicles, particularly in Bird's Eye View (BEV) feature extraction. wall1688/bevfusion-voxelization-sycl, https://github.com/wall1688/bevfusion-voxelization-sycl, fetched 2026-10-26 (unofficial) Zhaoyibinn/VGVGGT, https://github.com/Zhaoyibinn/VGVGGT, fetched 2026-10-27 (unofficial)

name: Dynamic Voxelization (Coordinate Only)
body: Dynamic Voxelization (Coordinate Only) computes the discrete voxel coordinates for each point in a point cloud without assigning them to a fixed-size voxel grid structure or handling duplicate merging. It is used when maxpoints is set to -1, effectively bypassing the aggregation and duplicate-handling stages of standard hard voxelization. Inputs and Outputs: Input: Point cloud coordinates tensor points of shape (N, D), where N is the number of points and D is the dimensionality (typically 3). Bounding box range R = [x{min}, y{min}, z{min}, x{max}, y{max}, z{max}] and voxel sizes v = [vx, vy, vz]. Output: Tensor coors of shape (N, D) containing the integer voxel indices for each point. Data Structures: points: Float tensor, shape (N, D). coors: Integer tensor, shape (N, D). griddims: Integer tuple (Gx, Gy, Gz) representing the dimensions of the bounding box in voxels. Parameters: NDim: Number of coordinate dimensions. Default is 3. maxpoints: Set to -1 to indicate coordinate-only mode. Steps: 1. Calculate Grid Dimensions: Compute the number of voxels along each axis using rounding: Gx = \text{round}\left(\frac{x{max} - x{min}}{vx}\right), \quad Gy = \text{round}\left(\frac{y{max} - y{min}}{vy}\right), \quad Gz = \text{round}\left(\frac{z{max} - z{min}}{vz}\right) 2. Compute Voxel Coordinates: For each point pn with coordinates (xn, yn, zn), compute the voxel index (in, jn, kn): in = \left\lfloor \frac{xn - x{min}}{vx} \right\rfloor, \quad jn = \left\lfloor \frac{yn - y{min}}{vy} \right\rfloor, \quad kn = \left\lfloor \frac{zn - z{min}}{vz} \right\rfloor 3. Boundary Handling: Points falling outside the bounding box R result in indices outside [0, Gx-1] \times [0, Gy-1] \times [0, Gz-1]. In this specific coordinate-only implementation, these points are stored as-is, as no duplicate merging or max-point limiting occurs. Pseudocode: Unverified code. The code below did not pass a test run against a reference implementation, or no test fits it, so it may contain errors. import math def dynamicvoxelizecoordinateonly(points, coorsrange, voxelsize, ndim=3): """ points: list of lists or tuples of shape (N, ndim) coorsrange: [xmin, ymin, zmin, xmax, ymax, zmax] voxelsize: [vx, vy, vz] returns: list of lists of shape (N, ndim) of integer voxel coordinates """ xmin, ymin, zmin, xmax, ymax, zmax = coorsrange vx, vy, vz = voxelsize # Calculate grid dimensions (computed per source, though not strictly used for coordinate mapping) gridx = round((xmax - xmin) / vx) gridy = round((ymax - ymin) / vy) gridz = round((zmax - zmin) / vz) # Initialize output list coors = [] # Compute voxel coordinates for each point for point in points: x, y = point[0], point[1] z = point[2] if ndim == 3 else 0.0 # Compute voxel indices using floor division i = math.floor((x - xmin) / vx) j = math.floor((y - ymin) / vy) k = math.floor((z - zmin) / vz) if ndim == 3 else 0 coors.append([i, j, k]) return coors Edge Cases and Pitfalls: Precision: Floating-point division and floor operations may cause points exactly on boundaries to be assigned to adjacent voxels depending on implementation details. Out-of-Bounds: Points outside the range R produce negative or excessive indices. Extends this method by adding feature aggregation and duplicate handling after coordinate computation. Choose when features need to be stored per voxel. Time Complexity: O(N), where N is the number of points, as each point is processed independently. Memory Complexity: O(N) for the output coordinate tensor. Strengths: Minimal memory overhead and fast execution, as it skips complex atomic operations and sorting required for duplicate handling. Limitations: Does not reduce point count; output size equals input size. When to use: When only spatial indexing is needed, or as a pre-processing step for more complex voxelization variants. This method is part of the dynamic voxelization pipeline used in 3D object detection frameworks, specifically implemented in CUDA for GPU acceleration. name: Dynamic Voxelization (Coordinate and Feature)
head: Dynamic Voxelization with Scatter Reduction
body: Dynamic Voxelization (Coordinate and Feature) converts point clouds to variable-size voxel grids, decomposed into coordinate calculation, indexing, and scatter-reduction stages. It differs from Dynamic Voxelization (Coordinate Only) by performing scatter-reduction on features during the voxelization process, rather than returning only coordinate mappings. The method processes a point cloud through three sequential stages. Input: Point cloud tensor P \in \mathbb{R}^{N \times D}, where N is the number of points and D is the feature dimension. Input: Voxelization parameters: voxel size v \in \mathbb{R}^3 and point cloud range R \in \mathbb{R}^6 (min/max x, y, z). Output: Voxel features tensor V \in \mathbb{R}^{K \times F}, where K is the number of non-empty voxels and F is the feature dimension. Output: Voxel coordinates tensor C \in \mathbb{R}^{K \times 3}, representing the grid indices of the non-empty voxels. Point Cloud: A flat tensor of shape (N, D). Voxel Coordinates: A tensor of shape (K, 3) storing integer grid indices (i, j, k) for each non-empty voxel. Routing Index: A 1D tensor of shape (N,) mapping each point to its target voxel index in the output feature tensor. 1. Calculate Target Coordinates: For each point pn = (xn, yn, zn, \dots), compute its voxel grid coordinates (in, jn, kn) using the voxel size v and range R: in = \left\lfloor \frac{xn - R{\min,x}}{vx} \right\rfloor, \quad jn = \left\lfloor \frac{yn - R{\min,y}}{vy} \right\rfloor, \quad kn = \left\lfloor \frac{zn - R{\min,z}}{vz} \right\rfloor Clamp coordinates to valid range [0, K{\max}-1] where K{\max} is derived from the range and voxel size. 2. Indexing: Calculate the non-empty coors set and routing information using torch.unique. This returns the unique voxel coordinates and an inverse index mapping each point to its target voxel row. 3. Scatter-Reduction: Dump pointwise features to voxelized features and perform reduction using scatteradd or equivalent. Unverified code. The code below did not pass a test run against a reference implementation, or no test fits it, so it may contain errors. import torch def dynamicvoxelizationandfeature( points: torch.Tensor, voxelsize: torch.Tensor, pointcloudrange: torch.Tensor, reduce: str = "sum") -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]: """ points: (N, D) tensor, D >= 3 voxelsize: (3,) tensor [vx, vy, vz] pointcloudrange: (6,) tensor [xmin, ymin, zmin, xmax, ymax, zmax] reduce: "sum" or "mean" Returns: coors: (K, 3) tensor of unique voxel coordinates features: (K, D) tensor of aggregated voxel features """ # Step 1: Calculate target coordinates shifted = points[:,:3] - pointcloudrange[:3] coorsfloat = shifted / voxelsize coorsint = torch.floor(coorsfloat).int() maxcoors = ((pointcloudrange[3:] - pointcloudrange[:3]) / voxelsize).int() coorsint = torch.clamp(coorsint, 0, maxcoors - 1) # Step 2: Indexing coorsunique, inverseindices = torch.unique( coorsint, dim=0, sorted=True, returninverse=True) K = coorsunique.shape[0] N = points.shape[0] D = points.shape[1] # Step 3: Scatter-Reduction (sum) features = torch.zeros((K, D), dtype=points.dtype, device=points.device) features.scatteradd(0, inverseindices.unsqueeze(1).expand(-1, D), points) if reduce == "mean": ones = torch.ones((N,), dtype=points.dtype, device=points.device) counts = torch.zeros((K,), dtype=points.dtype, device=points.device) counts.scatteradd(0, inverseindices, ones) counts = torch.clamp(counts, min=1) features = features / counts.unsqueeze(1) return coorsunique, features Not given in the sources. Extreme Density: Can be unstable when points are extremely dense, affecting voxelization efficiency. Redundant Indexing: Repeated scatter-reduces for the same point cloud require redundant indexing if not cached. Precision: Floating-point division in coordinate calculation may introduce small errors; clamping is essential to prevent out-of-bounds indices. Computes only voxel coordinates without feature aggregation. It sets itself apart by returning only coordinate mappings and skipping scatter-reduction. Use when maxpoints=-1 or when feature processing is handled separately. Link Assigns points to a fixed grid with max points per voxel. It sets itself apart by producing a deterministic output size and a fixed grid structure. Use when deterministic output size is required or for hardware acceleration. Link Time Complexity: Indexing (torch.unique) is the most computationally expensive part; scatter-reduction itself is fast. Memory Complexity: Not given in the sources. Performance: The indexing step dominates runtime. Strengths: Handles variable-size voxel grids efficiently. Limitations: Can be unstable when points are extremely dense. When to Use: Not given in the sources. When Not to Use: Not given in the sources. Dynamic Voxelization was discussed in the context of MMDetection3D implementation improvements, where contributors suggested dividing the dynamic scatter op into indexing and scatter-reduction parts to address performance bottlenecks. It was developed to provide a consistent implementation for 3D detection pipelines.
